title: The prayer as rest
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ said: give us rest by it, Bilal (Abu Dawud)

lines: I WISH I HAD PRAYED, AND RESTED.
BILAL, GIVE US REST BY IT.
cards: A man sitting with a few people says out loud that he wishes he had prayed, so he could have found some rest. The others seem to find that odd, and they let him know. Rest?
Prayer is a duty. You get it done. So he answers with something he heard the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say.
The report is in the Sunan of Abu Dawud. The Prophet would turn to Bilal, the man who called the prayer, and say: Bilal, call the iqamah, and give us rest by it. Not rest after it.

teach.h: ARIHNA BIHA: GIVE US REST BY IT.
teach.b: First, the Arabic the report gives: arihna biha. Give us rest by it, or with it. Some teachers point at that small word, biha, by it.

There's a way of praying that sounds like the opposite: give us rest from it, let's get this over with. The words in the report go the other way. The prayer isn't the task standing between you and your rest.
Second, the Qur'an puts it plainly in surah thirteen, in Pickthall's words: "Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!"

The prayer is remembrance in a body: standing, bowing, putting the forehead on the ground. Another report, in the Sunan of an-Nasa'i, has the Prophet ﷺ say that the comfort of his eye was placed in the prayer.
Comfort of the eye is an Arabic way of saying the thing you're glad to look at, the thing that settles you.
Third, look back at this week. The Friday sermon, heard in silence. The lighter prayer on the road.
Two prostrations when you forget, because mistakes are expected. One prostration of thanks at good news. A prayer for every kind of sky.
And yesterday, knowing what you say.
Each of those makes the prayer a little less like a test you pass and more like a room you walk into.

teach.h: VERILY IN THE REMEMBRANCE OF ALLAH DO HEARTS FIND REST!
teach.b: Fourth, an ordinary day. Several times a day the world stops asking you for things for a few minutes. The inbox can wait.
For Muslims, that pause is required, and the report says it was meant to feel like relief, not like one more thing on the list.

how: Muslims pray the daily prayers, and teachers sometimes recall the Prophet's words to Bilal, 'give us rest by it,' to encourage praying unhurried, as a relief rather than a chore.

games.q: what does “the prayer as rest” mean?
o: a short break allowed between the five daily prayers
resting after prayer before going back to work
prayer as relief: give us rest by it, not rest from it

games.q: the prayer as rest — tap the pairs.
p: the one asked to call the iqamah
what was placed in the prayer

s: the report says rest comes after the prayer is done
the words are give us rest by it: the prayer itself is the rest.
the Qur'an ties rest for the heart to the remembrance of Allah
"Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!" (13:28).
the man in the story was praised by everyone around him for wanting to pray
they seemed to find it odd, and he answered with the Prophet's words to Bilal.

games.q: it's time to pray, and the Prophet ﷺ turns to Bilal. what does the report say he asks for?
o: call it quickly, so we can be done with it.
call the iqamah, and give us rest by it.
wait until we have finished our work.
games.why: give us rest by it. the prayer isn't the thing between him and rest; it's where the rest is.

practice: If you pray, take your next prayer slowly, and in each position, standing, bowing, prostrating, let one thing you're carrying go down with you.
If you don't, breathe in and notice what you're holding, a task, a worry, a conversation, then breathe out and set it on the floor beside you. You don't have to finish anything.

wordCard.voice: The prayer as rest. Arihna biha: give us rest by it. The Prophet's words to Bilal, and the close of the prayer. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: give us rest by it, the Prophet's words to Bilal about the prayer (Abu Dawud).

carryVoice: Your line: rest in it. Tomorrow, a new pillar, and a word that means two things at once. Rest well.

sources.q: Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!
